messages:
sam: Hi all — I'm Sam, new to infra. Trying to open my first PR but fuzzy on branching + review etiquette. Quick Qs: branch naming conventions? squash vs merge? who to ping for runtime reviews? commit message format? thanks!
mira: welcome Sam! Branch naming we use: feat/<ticket>-short-desc, fix/<ticket>-short, chore/<what>. Example: feat/1764-reduce-kv-cache-mem
kevin: hey Sam :wave: PRs ideally <500 LOC. Small PRs = faster reviews. Squash on merge for bugfixes/quick things. For larger features keep history (don’t force-push after reviews start).
lina: commit msgs: follow Conventional Commits. One-line header like `feat(runtime): add delayed batching` + short body. Use `Co-authored-by:` if pairing.
jamal: reviewers: add the runtime owners (see CODEOWNERS) and `@eng-runtime`. For infra changes ping `@infra-eng`. Add `reviewer-needed` label to attract reviewers.
mira: our PR template also asks for tests, perf impact, and rollback notes — see .github/pull_request_template.md
sam: thanks! CI — what checks block merging?
CI-Bot: required checks: unit-tests, lint, e2e-if-modified, perf/regression. Branch protection blocks merge until green.
kevin: schema changes: include migration plan, rollback steps, and tag migration owners in PR. Add a short compatibility note.
lina: if PR touches production latency paths, add perf numbers and mention `@oncall` in the description for quick eyes.
mira: branching policy: long-lived feature branches should rebase onto main at least weekly. We prefer merge commits for release branches; squash for quick fixes.
sam: good call — any tips for making reviews go quicker?
jamal: put a tiny checklist at top: what changed, commands to run, files worth eyeballing. Example: `Areas to review: 1) kv cache eviction logic 2) batch scheduler` + `make test-infra`
mira: also label explicit reviewers in the GitHub UI, and if you need live help ping me or @devex. There's a 15-min PR office hours slot today at 16:00 if you want a walkthrough. :thumbsup:
